title: Microlocal Partition of Energy for Fractional-Type Dispersive Equations
version: arXiv:2309.15282v1, 26 September 2023, read in the TeX source (main/Introduction.tex and appendix/Appendix_Klein-Gordon_classical_truncation.tex). Published as Analysis & PDE 18 (2025), no. 9, 2081-2143, DOI 10.2140/apde.2025.18.2081; the published version was seen only through a search extract, where the items appear as Theorem 1.9, Remark 1.10, equation (1-32) and Appendix D. Numbering in v1 was not compiled.
locator: Introduction: the Klein-Gordon theorem (label eq_K-G_limit_of_energy) and the remark following it (label eq_K-G_limit_of_energy_classical); appendix section 'Partition of energy for Klein-Gordon equation: a classical setting', first 175 of 306 lines including the lemma labelled lem_K-G_classic_asymp and its proof
assumptions: Klein-Gordon equation (d_t^2 - Laplacian + 1) w = 0 on R^d, any d; real data w0 in H^1, w1 in L^2.
conclusion: Author's statement: for all 0 <= r0 <= r1 the energy in r0 < |x/t| < r1 converges as t -> +-infinity to the energy of the data frequency-localised to the momenta whose group velocity lies in (r0, r1); since group velocities lie in [0,1), the energy in |x| > |t| tends to 0.
proof_status: Proof read. It reduces to an asymptotic relation g(x/t)u(t) = g(-P'(D))u(t) + o(1) in L^2 for indicator functions of sets with null boundary, proved with a pseudo-differential cutoff. Two technical lemmas of the paper used for uniform L^2 bounds (labels lem_tech_change_of_x_and_xi, lem_tech_boundedness_of_symbol_study_in_xi) and an 'integration by parts' step were not read or re-derived. The last displayed line of the appendix computation swaps H^1 and L^2 norms relative to the remark; this looks like a misprint and does not affect the conclusion.
relevance: Supplies the exterior energy decay for finite-energy solutions in every space dimension, the estimate the massive-Minkowski note left unchecked.
open_questions: Whether the published version changed the statement or proof.
limits: m = 1 only (other m > 0 by scaling, my remark). Region |x| > |t| exactly, not |x| > |t| - R. Published version not compared.

title: Strengthened Reeh-Schlieder Property and Scattering in Quantum Field Theories without Mass Gaps
version: arXiv:1603.07512v2, 2 May 2017; Commun. Math. Phys. 352, 935-966 (2017), not compared. Sections 1-4 up to the statement of Theorem 9 read through a text extraction
locator: Section 3 (definition of regular positive-energy Klein-Gordon solution); Section 4, Lemma 6 (velocity-support estimate) and Corollary 7
assumptions: Three space dimensions; mass m >= 0; positive-energy solutions with smooth compactly supported momentum-space wave packet (for m = 0 also vanishing near k = 0).
conclusion: Author's Lemma 6: |f(t,x)| <= C_N / (delta^N |t|^N) when x/t lies at distance delta from the velocity support. Author's Corollary 7: f is rapidly decreasing in |t| + |x| outside any cone over a neighbourhood of the velocity support.
proof_status: Stated without proof. The author calls it a reformulation of a classical result of Ruelle (1962) and refers the non-stationary phase proof to Reed-Simon vol. III, Appendix 1 to XI.3, and to a textbook cited as [A] Thm. 5.3.
dependencies: Ruelle 1962; Reed and Simon III: not read.
relevance: A read statement of Lemma 2 of the note for n = 3, with attribution. The note proves Lemma 2 itself for all n.
limits: n = 3 and one frequency sign only. The rest of the paper was not read. Extraction through a third-party text service.

title: L^2 asymptotes for the Klein-Gordon equation
relevance: Abstract says an L^2 approximation to Klein-Gordon solutions is obtained from the Fourier transforms of the Cauchy data and 'applied to show how energy distributes among various conical regions'. Probably the earliest statement of the exterior energy decay.
limits: Abstract seen in a search result only. Author given there as S. A. Nelson; journal Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. inferred from the DOI. Dimension, hypotheses and the exact energy statement not verified.

limits: Not read. Robert S. Strichartz, J. Funct. Anal. 40 (1981) 341-357, details taken from Yang's bibliography file. Yang's criticism was read but not checked against the original.
